newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index slightly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index slightly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended Wednesday's morning session slightly lower on profit-taking although the A share market extended its recent strong gains, analysts said.
After solid rises over the past two days, the B share index fell 0.82 points or 0.45 percent to 183.37 on turnover of HK$87.8 million on Wednesday morning.
The domestic currency A share index rose 4.76 points or 0.91 percent to 529.97 on turnover of 10.90 billion yuan.
"Profit-taking eroded B share gains but the index is likely to hold steady in the afternoon before rising in the near future," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Both indices still show strong upward momentum over the medium term on the back of Beijing's solid economic forecast for the first half of 1997, analysts said.

China's gross domestic product is expected to grow 9.6 percent year-on-year in the first half of 1997, with retail price inflation seen at two percent, an official newspaper on Tuesday quoted a forecast by the State Economic and Trade Commission as saying.
New listings in Shenzhen scheduled for later this month are expected to further boost sentiment, brokers said.

Pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd and Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd have announced they will each offer 100 million B shares for listing this month.
"But some investors are holding back, waiting to see how the new shares perform," the Guotai analyst said.
Conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao (Group) Ltd was the biggest loser on the B share market, down HK$0.14 or 3.38 percent to HK$4.00.
On the A share market, Shenzhen Kaifa Techonology, which has a joint venture with International Business Machines Corp, was the worst performer, losing 3.56 yuan or 5.30 percent to 63.60 yuan.
